tools.name: agento11y_manage_agents
tools.description:
Read the agent catalog of Grafana Agent Observability (the grafana-agento11y-app plugin): which agents send telemetry, what their system prompts and tools are, how their prompt versions evolved, and how each version scored.

The catalog is derived from ingested telemetry, not from a registration step: an agent exists here once its generations have been seen. It answers "what is this agent", not "what did it do".

Operations:
- 'list': agents in this tenant, newest activity first. Each row carries the latest effective version, first and latest seen times, generation and version counts, tool count, a system prompt prefix, and token_estimate. Paginated via limit and cursor
- 'get': one agent version in full: the complete system prompt, every tool with its JSON schema, and the models it ran on. Returns the latest version unless 'version' is set
- 'list_versions': the version history of one agent, one row per effective version with its seen window, generation count, tool count, and token_estimate. Paginated
- 'list_version_scores': evaluation score aggregates per version, with per-evaluator score_key, pass and fail counts, and mean_score. Use it to compare how versions scored

Versions: an effective version is always 'sha256:<64 lowercase hex>', and only that form is accepted by 'get'; a declared version such as '1.4.2' is reported in the declared_version fields but cannot be looked up. The plugin derives the effective version from the first of these the telemetry carries: the version the SDK reported, a hash of the declared version, a hash of the system prompt. Adding, removing, or editing a tool never mints a new version. Editing the prompt mints one only for an agent that reports neither its own effective version nor a declared version, so an agent that declares '1.4.2' keeps one effective version across prompt edits.

Response size: 'get' returns the whole system prompt plus every tool schema, which can be tens of thousands of tokens. Check token_estimate.total from 'list' or 'list_versions' before fetching, and prefer the system_prompt_prefix in those rows when a prefix is enough.

Cross-referencing: an agent name from 'list' is the value of the agent = "<name>" filter in conversation search.

Pagination: when a response carries next_cursor, call the same operation again with cursor set to it. For 'list', also repeat the same name_prefix, start_time, and end_time using absolute RFC3339 times; the cursor is bound to those filters and a relative value such as now-7d or 7d re-resolves and is rejected.

Permissions: every operation is a read and needs grafana-agento11y-app.data:read (Agento11y Editor or Admin). This tool performs no writes.

When to use:
- Discovering which agent names exist before filtering conversations or generations by agent
- Reading the system prompt or tool inventory an agent ran with, or how they changed between versions
- Checking whether a new prompt version scores worse than the previous one

When NOT to use:
- Reading individual conversations, generations, or their scores
- Inspecting evaluators or the rules that schedule them

agent_name.description: Agent name from 'list'. Required for 'get', 'list_versions', and 'list_version_scores'. An explicitly empty string selects the unnamed agent (telemetry with no agent name), which 'get' and 'list_versions' accept and 'list_version_scores' rejects.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response's next_cursor, echoed back exactly (for 'list' and 'list_versions'). For 'list' also resend the same name_prefix, start_time, and end_time as the first call using absolute RFC3339 times; the cursor is bound to those filters and a relative value such as now-7d or 7d drifts between calls and is rejected.

end_time.description: End of the time range in RFC3339 or relative format (e.g. now). For 'list' it keeps agents last seen at or before this time and defaults to no upper bound. For 'list_version_scores' it ends the score window; passing it without start_time gives a 90-day window ending here.

limit.description: Maximum number of results per page (default 50, capped at 200 by the API) (for 'list' and 'list_versions')

name_prefix.description: Agent name filter (for 'list'). Despite the parameter name, the API matches it case-insensitively anywhere in the name, so 'agent' also returns 'my-agent'.

operation.description: The operation to perform: 'list' for the agent catalog, 'get' for one agent version in full (system prompt, tools, models), 'list_versions' for the version history of one agent, 'list_version_scores' for evaluation score aggregates per version

start_time.description: Start of the time range in RFC3339 or relative format (e.g. now-7d). For 'list' it keeps agents last seen at or after this time and defaults to no lower bound. For 'list_version_scores' it starts the score window; omitting it does not mean no lower bound, because the API then either scopes to the agent's 50 most recent versions or falls back to a 90-day window.

version.description: Effective version 'sha256:<64 lowercase hex>' from 'list' or 'list_versions', accepted only by 'get'. Omit it for the latest version. Declared versions such as '1.4.2' are not accepted here; they are reported in the declared_version fields.

tools.name: agento11y_manage_conversations
tools.description:
List, search, and fetch LLM conversations from Grafana Agent Observability (the grafana-agento11y-app plugin).

Operations:
- 'list': recent conversations (lightweight; id, title, generation count, timestamps), paginated via limit and cursor
- 'search': search conversations by filter expression and time range; results include models, agents, error counts, rating and eval summaries, and trace IDs
- 'get': one conversation by ID with all its generations, including full prompts and outputs (can be large)

Filter syntax for 'search': key operator value, with the value in double quotes; multiple filters are separated by spaces and combined with AND.
Filter keys (trace): model, provider, agent, agent.version, status, error.type, error.category, duration, tool.name, operation, namespace, cluster, service
Filter keys (metadata): generation_count, eval.passed, eval.evaluator_id, eval.score_key, eval.score
Operators: =, !=, >, <, >=, <=, =~ (regex)
Example: status = "error" agent = "claude-code"

Pagination: when a response has next_cursor, fetch the next page by calling the same operation again with cursor set to next_cursor. For 'search', also repeat the same filters, start_time, and end_time as the first call, using absolute RFC3339 times; relative ranges like now-24h shift between calls and the cursor will be rejected.

When to use:
- Debugging an AI application: find failing or low-rated conversations, then inspect their generations
- Reviewing evaluation results and user ratings across conversations

When NOT to use:
- Fetching a single generation or its evaluation scores

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response (for 'list' and 'search' operations). To fetch the next page set this to next_cursor. For 'search' also resend the same filters and start_time/end_time from the first call and use absolute RFC3339 times; relative ranges like now-24h invalidate the cursor.

end_time.description: End of the search time range in RFC3339 or relative format (e.g. now). Defaults to now (for 'search' operation)

filters.description: Filter expression (for 'search' operation). Format: key operator value with the value in double quotes, multiple filters separated by spaces. See the tool description for keys and operators.

limit.description: Maximum number of results per page (default 50) (for 'list' and 'search' operations)

operation.description: The operation to perform: 'list' for recent conversations, 'search' to filter conversations by expression and time range, 'get' to fetch one conversation with all its generations by ID

start_time.description: Start of the search time range in RFC3339 or relative format (e.g. now-6h). Defaults to now-24h (for 'search' operation)

tools.name: agento11y_manage_generations
tools.description:
Fetch a single LLM generation and its evaluation scores from Grafana Agent Observability (the grafana-agento11y-app plugin).

Operations:
- 'get': full generation detail by ID, including prompt, output, model, and usage (can be large)
- 'scores': evaluation scores for a generation (evaluator, score key, score type, value, passed, explanation)

When to use:
- Drilling into one generation of a conversation
- Checking why an evaluation passed or failed for a specific generation

When NOT to use:
- Searching or listing conversations

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response (for 'scores' operation)

limit.description: Maximum number of scores per page (default 50) (for 'scores' operation)

operation.description: The operation to perform: 'get' for the full generation detail, 'scores' for the evaluation scores of the generation

tools.name: alerting_manage_routing
tools.description:
Manage Grafana alerting routing configuration, including notification policies, contact points and time intervals.

Notification policies define how alerts are grouped, routed, and which contact points receive them.
Time intervals define active/mute periods for alert notifications.

When to use:
- Understanding how alerts are routed to contact points/receivers
- Debugging why an alert went to a specific receiver
- Checking grouping, timing, or mute interval settings

Does not show alert rule configuration or state.

contact_point_title.description: Title of the contact point to retrieve (required for get_contact_point operation)

datasource_uid.description: Optional: UID of an Alertmanager-compatible datasource to query for receivers. If omitted, returns Grafana-managed contact points. Only used with get_contact_points.

limit.description: The maximum number of results to return. Default is 100. Only used with get_contact_points.

name.description: Filter contact points by name (exact match). Only used with get_contact_points.

operation.description: The operation to perform: 'get_notification_policies' to retrieve the notification policy tree, 'get_contact_points' to list all contact points, 'get_contact_point' to get a specific contact point by name, 'get_time_intervals' to list all time intervals, 'get_time_interval' to get a specific time interval by name

time_interval_name.description: Name of the time interval to retrieve (required for get_time_interval operation)

tools.name: alerting_rules_read
tools.description:
List and inspect Grafana alert rules with filtering capabilities.

When to use:
- Understanding why an alert is or isn't firing
- Auditing alert rule configuration (queries, conditions, labels, notification settings)
- Finding alert rules by state, folder, group, or name
- Comparing rule versions to see what changed

Read-only: does not create, update, or delete rules, and does not show notification routing.

datasource_uid.description: Optional: UID of a Prometheus or Loki datasource to query for datasource-managed alert rules. If omitted, returns Grafana-managed rules.

folder_uid.description: Filter by exact folder UID (for 'list' operation). Mutually exclusive with search_folder.

label_selectors.description: Prometheus-style selectors to filter alert rules by labels. Each string is a selector e.g. '{severity="critical", team=~"backend.*"}'. All selectors must match (AND).

limit_alerts.description: Limit alert instances per rule. For list: 0 omits alerts. For get: <=0 defaults to 200. Max 200.

matchers.description: Label matchers to filter alert instances. Each string is a Prometheus-style matcher e.g. 'severity="critical"', 'env!="dev"', 'team=~"backend.*"'. Requires Grafana 12.4+.

operation.description: The operation to perform: 'list' to search/filter rules, 'get' to retrieve full rule details (state + configuration) by UID, or 'versions' to get the version history of a rule

rule_group.description: Filter by exact rule group name (for 'list' operation)

rule_limit.description: Maximum number of rules to return (default 200, max 200). Requires Grafana 12.4+ (for 'list' operation)

rule_uid.description: The UID of the alert rule (required for 'get' and 'versions' operations)

search_folder.description: Search folders by path using partial matching (for 'list' operation). Requires Grafana 12.4+. Mutually exclusive with folder_uid.

search_rule_name.description: Search alert rule names/titles using partial matching. Requires Grafana 12.4+ (for 'list' operation)

states.description: Filter by alert state: firing, pending, normal, recovering, nodata, error (for 'list' operation)

tools.name: alerting_silences_read
tools.description:
List and inspect Grafana alerting silences. A silence temporarily suppresses notifications for alerts whose labels match a set of matchers.

Operations:
- 'list': list existing silences. Optionally filter by rule_uid (matches the __alert_rule_uid__ label) or by matchers.
- 'get': retrieve a single silence by silence_id.

When to use:
- Inspecting which alerts are currently silenced and why

Read-only: does not create, update, or delete silences, and does not show alert rules or notification routing.

value.description: The label value to match against

isRegex.description: Whether value is a regular expression. Defaults to false.

isEqual.description: Whether the matcher asserts equality (true) or inequality (false). Defaults to true.

matchers.description: Optional label matchers used to filter listed silences. Only used with 'list'.

operation.description: The operation to perform: 'list' to list silences, 'get' to retrieve a silence by id

rule_uid.description: Optional: filter listed silences to those scoped to this alert rule UID (matches the __alert_rule_uid__ label). Only used with 'list'.

tools.name: analyze_loki_labels
tools.description: Audits a Loki label strategy and optionally diagnoses query performance. Returns per-label verdicts, missing base labels, normalisation issues, and a recommended set. Pass datasourceUid for live cardinality or labels for static scoring; both may be combined.

datasourceUid.description: Datasource UID (live mode).

perfMetrics.description: Runtime metrics; presence triggers perf diagnosis.

selector.description: Optional LogQL selector for stats / perf diagnosis.

tools.name: app_observability_handler
tools.description:
Inspect Application Observability services on this Grafana stack.

Commands: list finds services across Knowledge Graph scopes; get reports one service's RED metrics and topology; operations lists one service's native operations; dependencies reports its upstream callers or downstream services; quality reports instrumentation checks; runtime reports JVM or Node.js runtime metrics. Service inventory, identity, topology, quality, and runtime metadata require an active Knowledge Graph and Application Observability integration. Native operation metrics come from the configured Prometheus datasource and do not require Knowledge Graph. The optional namespace for native operations is a Prometheus job prefix, which may differ from a Knowledge Graph namespace. Results include links into the app.

command.description: list (every service) | get (RED KPIs for one service) | operations (RED KPIs per operation under one service) | dependencies (services upstream/downstream of one service) | quality (Knowledge Graph instrumentation-quality report for one service) | runtime (JVM/Node.js runtime metrics for one service)

datasourceUid.description: Pin the Prometheus datasource holding the App O11y metrics, when the tool reports several candidates

direction.description: For dependencies: upstream (callers of the service) or downstream (services it calls). Defaults to downstream.

env.description: Knowledge Graph environment scope for list, get, dependencies, quality, or runtime. For runtime it selects service metadata but does not filter native metrics.

limit.description: For list, operations, and dependencies: cap rows after sorting, up to 50.

namespace.description: For list, get, dependencies, quality, and runtime: Knowledge Graph Service namespace scope, which need not equal the Kubernetes namespace, OTel service.namespace, or native job prefix. For operations: prefix of the native Prometheus job label (<namespace>/<service>).

service.description: Service name (required for get, operations, dependencies, quality, runtime; from the list command)

site.description: Knowledge Graph site scope for list, get, dependencies, quality, or runtime. For runtime it selects service metadata but does not filter native metrics.

sortBy.description: For list, operations, and dependencies: sort rows by request rate, error ratio, p95 latency, or name. Unset preserves the default order.

sortDirection.description: Sort direction for sortBy. Defaults to desc for RED metrics and asc for name.

tools.name: app_observability_operation_handler
tools.description:
Inspect Application Observability operations on this Grafana stack.

Commands: top ranks operations across services by latency, errors, or request rate; get reports full RED metrics, including p99 latency, for one service and operationName. Both commands read native Prometheus span metrics independently of Knowledge Graph. The optional namespace is the native Prometheus job prefix, which may differ from a Knowledge Graph namespace. Results include links into the app.

command.description: top (slowest/highest-error/busiest operations across every service, unscoped to any one service) | get (full RED KPIs, including p99, for one already-identified operation under one service)

datasourceUid.description: Pin the Prometheus datasource holding the App O11y metrics, when the tool reports several candidates

limit.description: For top: cap the number of rows returned, applied after sorting. Defaults to 10 — this is a small triage view of the worst offenders, not a full inventory dump. Maximum 50.

namespace.description: Native Prometheus job prefix, not Knowledge Graph scope. For top: match jobs beginning <namespace>/; for get: select job <namespace>/<service>. It may differ from Kubernetes or OTel service namespace.

operation.description: Legacy direct-tool input for the operation/span name.

operationName.description: Required for get: the exact operation/span name to look up.

service.description: Required for get: the service the operation belongs to.

sortBy.description: For top: sort by request rate, error ratio, or p95 latency. Defaults to p95 (slowest first).

sortDirection.description: For top: sort direction. Defaults to desc (worst/busiest first).

tools.name: assistant_search
tools.description:
Historical/indexed memory search across your Grafana stack: infrastructure/service groups, dashboards, past investigations, mostly-resolved IRM incidents, and alert-rule definitions.

Covers architecture, topology, dashboard discovery (including panel queries), alerts by meaning or content, past incidents, past investigations/RCAs, and broad "what do we know about X?" questions. Investigation and incident searches default to records created in the last three calendar months.

Results are indexed snapshots, not live telemetry, and can be stale or incomplete: an infrastructure result's dependency list comes from a sample of recent traces and can miss calls. Live metrics, logs, traces, alert state, and on-call or incident data are not searched.

Returns results grouped by collection with titles, summaries, links, and metadata (including datasource UIDs for infrastructure results).

collections.description: Required, non-empty set of collections to search; there is no search-all value. dashboards: dashboards and their panel queries. alertRules: alert rule definitions. incidents: past incidents. investigations: past investigations and RCAs. infrastructure: indexed architecture, topology, and stored datasource mappings. Listing all five includes infrastructure.

endTime.description: Exclusive investigation and incident creation-time upper bound (RFC3339). Must be after startTime when both are supplied.

limits.description: Optional positive integer retrieval limits keyed by dashboards, infrastructure, investigations, incidents, or alertRules. Omitted entries keep existing defaults (20 dashboards, 3 infrastructure, 5 investigations, 5 incidents; alert rules use their retrieval limit). Limits are passed to collection retrieval backends, with no post-retrieval truncation. Filtering and deduplication may return fewer matches.

alertRules.description: Maximum alert-rule results, from 1 to 200. Omit to retain the existing retrieval limit of 20 alert rules.

dashboards.description: Maximum dashboard results, from 1 to 200. Omit to retain 20 dashboards.

incidents.description: Maximum incident results, from 1 to 200. Omit to retain 5 incidents.

infrastructure.description: Maximum infrastructure results, from 1 to 200. Omit to retain 3 infrastructure memories.

investigations.description: Maximum investigation results, from 1 to 200. Omit to retain 5 investigations.

query.description: A natural-language search query describing what to find across infrastructure/service groups, dashboards, past investigations, incidents, and alert rules. Service names, error messages, and symptoms improve results.

startTime.description: Inclusive investigation and incident creation-time lower bound (RFC3339). Defaults to the start of the last three calendar months.

tools.name: check_datasources_health
tools.description: Check datasource health. Filter by type or UIDs; omit both to check all.

type.description: Plugin type filter; omit to check all

tools.name: describe_sql_table
tools.description: Get column schema for a table in a supported SQL datasource (ClickHouse, Snowflake, Athena, MySQL, PostgreSQL, MSSQL). Returns column names and types.

database.description: Database name. Behavior varies by datasource type.

datasourceUid.description: The UID of the SQL datasource.

tools.name: diff_tempo_traces
tools.description: Compare two complete traces. Returns a compact summary and includes the full span-level patch when it is at most 64 KiB. Request trace-patch-v0 only when full details are required; full patches are not size-bounded.

base_end.description: Optional end of the baseline trace search range in RFC3339 format. Must be provided with base_start.

base_start.description: Optional start of the baseline trace search range in RFC3339 format. Must be provided with base_end.

base_trace_id.description: Trace ID for the baseline trace

compare_end.description: Optional end of the comparison trace search range in RFC3339 format. Must be provided with compare_start.

compare_start.description: Optional start of the comparison trace search range in RFC3339 format. Must be provided with compare_end.

compare_trace_id.description: Trace ID for the comparison trace

datasourceUid.description: UID of the tempo datasource to query

format.description: Output format. The composed format returns a compact summary and attaches the full patch only when it is at most 64 KiB. trace-patch-v0 has no output-size guarantee.

tools.name: frontend_observability_handler
tools.description:
Inspect Frontend Observability apps and browser telemetry on this Grafana stack.

Commands: list returns paginated app summaries and links; get returns one app by appId; web-vitals reports Core Web Vitals by page; errors ranks browser error groups with page and error links. App IDs are available from list. Creating an app requires a grant with grafana:write.

appId.description: The ID of the Frontend Observability app (required for get, web-vitals, and errors commands)

command.description: Read command: list apps, get an app, report web-vitals, or rank errors.

datasourceUid.description: UID of the Loki datasource holding this app's Faro telemetry. Only needed when web-vitals or errors reports that resolution was ambiguous — it names the candidates.

limit.description: Maximum results for list (default 50, integer) or errors (default 10), max 50

offset.description: Zero-based offset in the filtered app list for list (default 0).

pageId.description: Filter to a single page path, e.g. "/checkout" (optional for web-vitals and errors commands)

query.description: Case-insensitive app name substring for list.

rangeHours.description: Lookback window in hours for the web-vitals and errors commands (default 24)

tools.name: get_alert_group
tools.description: Get a specific alert group from Grafana OnCall by its ID. Returns the full alert group details, including the most recent alert and its raw payload when the OnCall API provides them. Alert payloads carry integration-specific fingerprints (for example Sentry's payload.data.event.hashes or Alertmanager's payload.alerts[].fingerprint) that identify recurring alerts across different alert groups.

alertGroupId.description: The ID of the alert group to retrieve

tools.name: get_annotation_tags
tools.description: Returns annotation tags with optional filtering by tag name. Only the provided filters are applied.

limit.description: Max results, default 100

tools.name: get_annotations
tools.description: Fetch Grafana annotations using filters such as dashboard UID, time range and tags.

limit.description: Max results default 100

matchAny.description: If true, match any tag (OR). If false, match all tags (AND). Default: false

tags.description: Filter by tags. Multiple tags allowed; use matchAny to control AND/OR logic

tools.name: get_assertions
tools.description: Get assertion summary for a given entity with its type, name, env, site, namespace, and a time range

endTime.description: The end time in RFC3339 format (e.g. 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z) or relative format (e.g. now)

entityName.description: The name of the entity to list

entityType.description: The type of the entity to list (e.g. Service, Node, Pod, etc.)

env.description: The env of the entity to list

namespace.description: The namespace of the entity to list

site.description: The site of the entity to list

startTime.description: The start time in RFC3339 format (e.g. 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z) or relative format (e.g. now-1h)

tools.name: get_assistant_conversation
tools.description:
Read the transcript of an existing Grafana Assistant conversation by ID.

Covers conversations started anywhere, including the Assistant sidebar in Grafana. Returns the user-visible messages in order as prose; includeToolCalls adds the assistant's tool calls and results.

The conversationId is the same identifier used as an Assistant conversation's contextId.

conversationId.description: The conversation ID to read; the same identifier as an Assistant conversation's contextId.

includeToolCalls.description: Optional. Include the assistant's tool calls and tool results in the transcript. Defaults to false (prose only).

tools.name: get_current_oncall_users
tools.description: Get the list of users currently on-call for a specific Grafana OnCall schedule ID. Returns the schedule ID, name, and a list of detailed user objects for those currently on call.

scheduleId.description: The ID of the schedule to get current on-call users for

tools.name: get_dashboard_by_uid
tools.description: Retrieves the complete dashboard, including panels, variables, and settings, for a specific dashboard identified by its UID. Pass optional version to load a saved snapshot instead of the current dashboard. Saved snapshots are fetched through Grafana's legacy versions API, so 'apiVersion' is omitted and 'meta' is partial: only version, createdBy, and created are populated. For current (non-versioned) fetches, the response includes 'apiVersion' and 'isV2': when 'isV2' is true the dashboard uses the v2 schema (panels live under 'elements' keyed by name, arranged by 'layout'; variables under 'variables'), otherwise it is classic v1 ('panels[]' with 'templating.list'). The full JSON of a large dashboard can be very large.

version.description: Optional saved version. Omit for the current dashboard

tools.name: get_dashboard_panel_queries
tools.description: Retrieve panel queries from a Grafana dashboard. Supports all datasource types (Prometheus, Loki, CloudWatch, SQL, etc.) and row-nested panels. Optionally filter to a specific panel by ID with `panelId`. Optionally provide `variables` for template variable substitution, which populates `processedQuery` and `requiredVariables` fields. Returns an array of objects with fields: title, query (raw expression), datasource (object with uid and type), and optionally processedQuery, refId, requiredVariables, and target. Targets built in a visual editor (CloudWatch metric search, InfluxDB query builder) have no string expression: those return an empty query plus `target`, the panel's raw query JSON. They can be executed as panel queries but not as standalone expressions.

panelId.description: Optional panel ID to filter to a specific panel

tools.name: get_dashboard_property
tools.description: Get specific parts of a dashboard using JSONPath expressions to minimize context window usage. JSONPath targets the dashboard's native schema. Classic v1 paths: '$.title' (title), '$.panels[*].title' (all panel titles), '$.panels[0]' (first panel), '$.templating.list' (variables), '$.annotations.list' (saved dashboard annotation queries/definitions), '$.tags' (tags), '$.panels[*].targets[*].expr' (all queries). v2 dashboards (isV2 true) use different paths: '$.title', '$.elements' (panels, keyed by name), '$.variables' (variables), '$.annotations'.

jsonPath.description: JSONPath expression to extract specific data (e.g., '$.panels[0].title' for first panel title, '$.panels[*].title' for all panel titles, '$.templating.list' for variables, '$.annotations.list' for saved dashboard annotation queries/definitions)

tools.name: get_dashboard_summary
tools.description: Get a compact summary of a dashboard including title, panel count, panel types, variables, and other metadata without the full JSON. Use this for dashboard overview and planning modifications without consuming large context windows.

tools.name: get_datasource
tools.description: Retrieves detailed information about a specific datasource by UID or name. Returns the full datasource model, including name, type, URL, access settings, JSON data, and secure JSON field status. Provide either uid or name; uid takes priority if both are given.

name.description: The name of the datasource. Used if UID is not provided.

uid.description: The UID of the datasource. If provided, takes priority over name.

tools.name: get_doc
tools.description: Fetch a Grafana documentation page. Set outline_only=true to get the heading structure first, then call again with a section name for bounded retrieval.

limit.description: Max lines to return (default ~80)

outline_only.description: Return only the heading outline (use to discover section names before fetching content)

section.description: Heading text to extract (returns only that section)

tools.name: get_incident
tools.description: Get a single incident by ID. Returns the full incident details including title, status, severity, labels, custom fields, timestamps, and other metadata.

id.description: The ID of the incident to retrieve

tools.name: get_investigation
tools.description:
Get one Grafana Assistant investigation (AI-driven root-cause investigation) by ID.

Returns the investigation's identifiers (investigationId and chatId), the authoritative row lifecycle state and metadata (title, description, state, summary, labels, team ownership, timestamps, completion quality, failure details), and the engine work snapshot (sessionStatus, mode, epoch, plan, report content).

The row's state field is authoritative for investigation lifecycle (pending, in_progress, completed, failed, cancelled, paused). The snapshot's sessionStatus only describes the engine session (idle, active, pause) and does not indicate completion or failure. Legacy (v1) investigations may have no snapshot; the row metadata is still returned with snapshotError set.

tools.name: get_investigation_report
tools.description:
Read the report of one Grafana Assistant investigation (AI-driven root-cause investigation) as markdown.

Returns the report plus the investigation's state, summary, completion quality, reportPending, and a url to open it in Grafana. The report is empty until the investigation writes one, which usually happens once it settles. An investigation can also settle without a report, for example when it answers directly; its summary then holds the answer. A follow-up turn can regenerate the report, in which case reportPending is true and the previous report is returned.

Reports cite evidence with [cite:pN] markers, and embedded panels appear as the same markers. Each marker is a panel ID in the investigation's evidence index.

tools.name: get_investigation_thread
tools.description:
Get the working thread of one Grafana Assistant investigation (AI-driven root-cause investigation) by ID: the user-visible conversation between the investigation agent and its tools.

Resolves the investigation to its backing chat and returns the non-hidden user-visible messages in order. Each message keeps only prose (the agent's narrative and findings), tool calls (toolName and toolInput), and tool results (raw query output); internal reasoning and bookkeeping blocks are excluded. Tool results are returned verbatim and can be large; limit and offset page through long threads, and total reports the full user-visible count.

The thread holds the raw data behind a report's [cite:pN] citations: each evidence entry's toolUseId matches the tool_result block in this thread that holds the captured query output.

limit.description: Maximum number of messages to return. 0 or omitted returns all.

offset.description: Number of user-visible messages to skip from the start of the thread.

tools.name: get_oncall_shift
tools.description: Get detailed information for a specific Grafana OnCall shift using its ID. A shift represents a designated time period within a schedule when users are actively on-call. Returns the full shift details.

shiftId.description: The ID of the shift to get details for

tools.name: get_panel_image
tools.description: Render a Grafana dashboard panel, full dashboard or Explore view as a PNG image. Returns the image as base64 encoded data. Requires the Grafana Image Renderer service to be installed. Exactly one of dashboardUid (for stored dashboards), provisioningPreview (for dashboards staged on a provisioning repository branch, e.g. a git-sync PR) or explore (an ad-hoc datasource query rendered in Explore, no saved dashboard needed) must be supplied. Use this for generating visual snapshots of dashboards for reports, alerts, or presentations.

dashboardUid.description: The UID of a stored dashboard containing the panel. Required unless provisioningPreview is provided.

datasourceUid.description: Datasource UID to query

explore.description: Render an ad-hoc Explore view for a datasource and queries instead of a stored dashboard. Mutually exclusive with dashboardUid and provisioningPreview. Requires Grafana 10.2 or later.

height.description: Height of the rendered image in pixels. Defaults to 500 (1000 for explore)

panelId.description: The ID of the panel to render. If omitted, the entire dashboard is rendered

repo.description: Provisioning repository slug. List repositories via /apis/provisioning.grafana.app/v0alpha1/namespaces/default/repositories if unknown.

path.description: Path to the dashboard file within the repository, relative to its root.

ref.description: Branch or commit SHA to render from. Defaults to the repository's main branch when omitted.

provisioningPreview.description: Render a dashboard from a provisioning repository branch (e.g. a git-sync PR preview). Mutually exclusive with dashboardUid.

scale.description: Scale factor for the image (1-3). Defaults to 1

theme.description: Theme for the rendered image: light or dark. Defaults to dark

timeRange.description: Time range for the rendered image

timeout.description: Rendering timeout in seconds. Defaults to 60

variables.description: Dashboard variables to apply. Values can be a single string or an array of strings for multi-value variables (e.g., {"var-datasource": "prometheus", "var-instance": ["server1", "server2"]})

width.description: Width of the rendered image in pixels. Defaults to 1000

tools.name: get_plugin

tools.name: get_query_examples
tools.description: Get example queries for a specific datasource type. datasourceType.description: The datasource type to get examples for (e.g. 'prometheus', 'loki', 'clickhouse', 'cloudwatch', 'influxdb')

tools.name: get_resource_description
tools.description: List available permissions and assignment capabilities for a Grafana resource type.

resourceType.description: Type of Grafana resource to get description for

tools.name: get_resource_permissions
tools.description: List all permissions set on a specific Grafana resource (e.g., dashboard, datasource, folder) by its type and ID.

resourceId.description: Unique identifier of the resource (UID for dashboards/datasources/folders)

tools.name: get_role_assignments
tools.description: List all assignments for a specific role, showing which users, teams, and service accounts have been assigned this role.

tools.name: get_role_details
tools.description: Get detailed information about a specific Grafana role by its UID, including permissions, metadata, and configuration.

tools.name: get_snapshot

tools.name: get_tempo_trace
tools.description: Retrieve a specific trace by ID

focus_span_id.description: Optional 16-character hexadecimal span ID to select initially. The full trace remains available.

tools.name: get_tempo_traceql_docs

topic.description: Which section of the TraceQL reference to retrieve: 'basic' for attribute and duration filters, 'aggregates' for count/avg/sum and by() grouping, 'structural' for parent/child and descendant operators, 'metrics' for rate/quantile_over_time metrics queries

tools.name: kubernetes_handler
tools.description:
Inspect the Kubernetes Monitoring inventory on this Grafana stack.

The read-only list and get commands resolve the same levels: omit cluster for clusters, set cluster for namespaces, add namespace for Deployments, and add workload for pods of that Deployment. An optional datasourceUid selects a Prometheus datasource. The app must be installed and activated, and the caller needs the Kubernetes Monitoring read action for the requested level. Results include links into the app.

cluster.description: Cluster name (required for get; from the list command)

command.description: list (all clusters with their node, namespace and pod counts) or get (drill into one cluster, namespace, or Deployment)

datasourceUid.description: Pin the Prometheus datasource holding the cluster metrics, when the tool reports several candidates

namespace.description: Namespace within the cluster (optional for get)

workload.description: Deployment name within the namespace (optional for get; lists that workload's pods)

tools.name: list_alert_groups
tools.description: List alert groups from Grafana OnCall with filtering options. Supports filtering by alert group ID, route ID, integration ID, state (new, acknowledged, resolved, silenced), team ID, time range, labels, and name. For time ranges, use format '{start}_{end}' ISO 8601 timestamp range (e.g., '2025-01-19T00:00:00_2025-01-19T23:59:59' for a specific day). For labels, use format 'key:value' (e.g., ['env:prod', 'severity:high']). Returns a list of alert group objects with their details. Supports pagination.

id.description: Filter by specific alert group ID

labels.description: Filter by labels in format key:value (e.g., ['env:prod', 'severity:high'])

startedAt.description: Filter by time range in format '{start}_{end}' ISO 8601 timestamp range (UTC assumed, no timezone indicator needed) (e.g., '2025-01-19T00:00:00_2025-01-19T23:59:59')

state.description: Filter by alert group state (one of: new, acknowledged, resolved, silenced)

tools.name: list_all_roles
tools.description: List all roles in Grafana. Optionally filter to show only roles that can be delegated by the current user. Returns role details including UID, name, permissions, and metadata.

delegatableOnly.description: Optional: If set true only return roles that can be delegated by current user

tools.name: list_cloudwatch_dimension_values
tools.description: List values for a CloudWatch dimension key (e.g. the specific cluster names behind a ClusterName dimension). Requires region. Supports cross-account monitoring via optional accountId parameter.

datasourceUid.description: The UID of the CloudWatch datasource

dimensionKey.description: Dimension key to list values for (e.g. ClusterName)

tools.name: list_cloudwatch_dimensions
tools.description: List dimension keys for a CloudWatch metric. Requires region. Supports cross-account monitoring via optional accountId parameter.

datasourceUid.description: The UID of the CloudWatch datasource

tools.name: list_cloudwatch_metrics
tools.description: List metrics for a CloudWatch namespace. Requires region. Supports cross-account monitoring via optional accountId parameter.

datasourceUid.description: The UID of the CloudWatch datasource

tools.name: list_cloudwatch_namespaces
tools.description: List available CloudWatch namespaces (AWS/EC2, AWS/ECS, AWS/RDS, etc.). Requires region. Supports cross-account monitoring via optional accountId parameter.

tools.name: list_dashboard_versions

tools.name: list_datasources
tools.description: List all configured datasources in Grafana. Use this to discover available datasources and their UIDs. Supports filtering by type and/or name (case-insensitive substring match) and pagination.

type.description: The type of datasources to search for. For example, 'prometheus', 'loki', 'tempo', etc...

tools.name: list_graphite_metrics
tools.description: Discover available metric paths in a Graphite datasource by browsing the metric tree. datasourceUid.description: The UID of the Graphite datasource to query

tools.name: list_graphite_tags
tools.description: List available tag names in a Graphite datasource that uses tag-based metrics. Returns a list of tag name strings (e.g. ["name", "env", "region"]). datasourceUid.description: The UID of the Graphite datasource to query

tools.name: list_incident_custom_fields
tools.description: List the custom fields configured for Grafana incidents, including their type and, for select fields, the options that may be chosen.

tools.name: list_incidents
tools.description: List Grafana incidents. Allows filtering by status ('active', 'resolved') and optionally including drill incidents. Returns a preview list with basic details, and custom field values if requested.

includeCustomFields.description: Whether to include each incident's custom field values. Off by default because it costs an extra request and makes the response considerably larger

limit.description: The maximum number of incidents to return

status.description: The status of the incidents to include. Valid values: 'active', 'resolved'

tools.name: list_investigation_evidence
tools.description:
List the evidence citation index for one Grafana Assistant investigation (AI-driven root-cause investigation) by ID.

Investigation reports cite captured query panels with [cite:pN] markers. Each evidence entry describes one captured panel, keyed by that panel ID: the tool that produced it (prometheus, loki, tempo, pyroscope), a human-readable query summary, the epoch (agent turn) at capture time, the capture timestamp, and the tool call ID that produced it.

This is an index, not the data: raw query results live in the investigation thread, in the tool result whose ID matches the entry's toolUseId. Legacy (v1) investigations have no engine session and return an empty list.

tools.name: list_investigation_profiles
tools.description:
List the agent profiles available for Grafana Assistant investigations (AI-driven root-cause investigations) on this Grafana Cloud stack.

Each profile describes an investigation agent configuration: its ID, display name, description, whether it is the default, its step budget, the tools it can use, and its content hash. A profile's ID is the agentProfileId accepted when creating an investigation.

tools.name: list_investigations
tools.description:
List Grafana Assistant investigations (AI-driven root-cause investigations) on this Grafana Cloud stack.

Returns one summary per investigation — ID, chat ID, title, state, timestamps, labels, team ownership, progress, and completion quality — plus the total count of matches for pagination. Results are limited to investigations the authenticated user is allowed to see.

All filters are optional. chatId finds the investigation that owns a known chat (all other filters are then ignored), q is free-text search, state/scope/label/teamName/from/to narrow results, and limit/offset with the returned total paginate.

archivedOnly.description: Return only investigations whose backing chat is archived. Overrides includeArchived when true.

chatId.description: Find the investigation owning this chat ID. Returns a singleton (or empty) list. When set, all other filters are ignored.

from.description: Only investigations created at or after this RFC3339 timestamp.

includeArchived.description: Include investigations whose backing chat is archived.

includeLegacy.description: Also include legacy (v1) investigations in results.

label.description: Filter by label in key:value format.

limit.description: Maximum number of investigations to return.

offset.description: Number of investigations to skip, for pagination.

q.description: Search text matched against investigation title, description, or chat name.

scope.description: Visibility scope: all, mine, teams, or system.

sort.description: Sort field: createdAt, updatedAt, title, or state.

state.description: Filter by investigation state: pending, in_progress, completed, failed, cancelled, or paused.

teamName.description: Filter investigations to a specific team by name.

to.description: Only investigations created at or before this RFC3339 timestamp.

tools.name: list_loki_label_names
tools.description: Lists all available label/field names (keys) found in logs within a specified Loki or VictoriaLogs datasource and time range. datasourceUid.description: The UID of the datasource to query

endRfc3339.description: Optionally, the end time of the query in RFC3339 format or relative time (e.g. 'now') (defaults to now)

matcher.description: Optionally, a stream selector to narrow the search to matching streams (Loki: LogQL, e.g. '{namespace="prod"}'; VictoriaLogs: LogsQL). Defaults to searching across all streams.

startRfc3339.description: Optionally, the start time of the query in RFC3339 format or relative time (e.g. 'now-1h') (defaults to 1 hour ago)

tools.name: list_loki_label_values
tools.description: Retrieves all unique values associated with a specific `labelName` within a Loki or VictoriaLogs datasource and time range. Returns a list of string values (e.g., for `labelName="env"`, might return `["prod", "staging", "dev"]`). Useful for discovering filter options. Defaults to the last hour if the time range is omitted. Optionally narrow the search to a subset of streams with `matcher` (e.g. `{namespace="prod"}`) — for example, to list `service` values seen only within a specific namespace.

datasourceUid.description: The UID of the datasource to query

endRfc3339.description: Optionally, the end time of the query in RFC3339 format or relative time (e.g. 'now') (defaults to now)

labelName.description: The name of the label to retrieve values for (e.g. 'app', 'env', 'pod')

matcher.description: Optionally, a stream selector to narrow the search to matching streams (Loki: LogQL, e.g. '{namespace="prod"}'; VictoriaLogs: LogsQL). Defaults to searching across all streams.

startRfc3339.description: Optionally, the start time of the query in RFC3339 format or relative time (e.g. 'now-1h') (defaults to 1 hour ago)

tools.name: list_oncall_schedules
tools.description: List Grafana OnCall schedules, optionally filtering by team ID. If a specific schedule ID is provided, retrieves details for only that schedule. Returns a list of schedule summaries including ID, name, team ID, timezone, and shift IDs. Supports pagination.

scheduleId.description: The ID of the schedule to get details for. If provided, returns only that schedule's details

teamId.description: The ID of the team to list schedules for

tools.name: list_oncall_teams
tools.description: List teams configured in Grafana OnCall. Returns a list of team objects with their details. Supports pagination.

tools.name: list_oncall_users
tools.description: List users from Grafana OnCall. These are OnCall users (separate from Grafana users). Can retrieve all users in the OnCall directory, a specific user by ID, or filter by username. Returns a list of user objects with their details. Supports pagination.

tools.name: list_prometheus_label_names

data_source_uid.description: The UID of the datasource to query

is not provided, it defaults to the last hour.

end_rfc_3339.description: Optionally, the end time of the query in RFC3339 format or relative time (e.g. 'now') (defaults to now)

matchers.description: Optionally, Prometheus style matchers used to filter the result set (defaults to: {})

start_rfc_3339.description: Optionally, the start time of the query in RFC3339 format or relative time (e.g. 'now-1h') (defaults to 1 hour ago)

tools.name: list_tempo_attribute_names
tools.description: List available attribute names for TraceQL queries. Without a scope (resource, span, etc.) the response can be very large.

datasourceUid.description: UID of the tempo datasource to query

Common namespaces: AWS/EC2, AWS/ECS, AWS/RDS, AWS/Lambda, ECS/ContainerInsights

Example dimensions: ECS: {ClusterName, ServiceName}, EC2: {InstanceId}

Cross-account monitoring: Use accountId to query metrics from a specific source account (e.g. '123456789012') or 'all' to query all linked accounts. Only applicable when using a CloudWatch monitoring account datasource.

accountId.description: AWS account ID for cross-account monitoring. Specify an account ID to query metrics from a specific source account, or 'all' to query all accounts the monitoring account is permitted to query. Only relevant when using a CloudWatch monitoring account datasource.

datasourceUid.description: The UID of the CloudWatch datasource to query.

end.description: End time. Formats: 'now', '2026-02-02T20:00:00Z', '1738522800000' (Unix ms). Default: now

namespace.description: CloudWatch namespace (e.g. AWS/ECS, AWS/EC2, AWS/RDS, AWS/Lambda)

start.description: Start time. Formats: 'now-1h', '2026-02-02T19:00:00Z', '1738519200000' (Unix ms). Default: now-1h

statistic.description: Statistic type: Average, Sum, Maximum, Minimum, SampleCount, or a percentile such as p50, p95 or p99.9. Default: Average

tools.name: query_elasticsearch
tools.description: Executes a search query against an Elasticsearch or OpenSearch datasource and retrieves matching documents. Supports Lucene query syntax (e.g., 'status:200 AND host:server1') for both Elasticsearch and OpenSearch. Elasticsearch Query DSL JSON is also supported for Elasticsearch datasources only (not OpenSearch). Returns a list of documents with their index, ID, source fields, and optional score. Use this to search logs, metrics, or any indexed data stored in Elasticsearch or OpenSearch. Defaults to 10 results and sorts by @timestamp in descending order (newest first).
